subject: Lyra evaluation - DPA request, SCC module guidance & questionnaire
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varga <elena@lyra.ai>, Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@lyra.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Lyra evaluation - DPA request, SCC module guidance & questionnaire

Hi Elena / Marcus —

Great to meet earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so procurement and legal teams have what they need. Short version: Lyra is a good fit for the pilot but we need to align on data roles/SCC choice and get your completed vendor questionnaire so our legal + security can finish the review.

Recap from the call:
- Primary scope: Lyra will route user prompts to Redwood-hosted inference for a secure, latency-sensitive feature. No telemetry is stored beyond ephemeral KV cache (customer-controlled retention).
- Compliance asks you raised: SOC 2 status, HIPAA applicability for a subset of customers, DPA / SCC selection, and audit log access.
- Timeline: you indicated a procurement decision target of end of July.

What we need from Lyra:
1) Completed vendor security questionnaire (I attached a Lyra-friendly stub in case you prefer it).
2) Confirmation on whether Lyra will be Controller for the data sent to the model (our default assumption) or whether there are feature flows where Redwood would act as Controller for generated artifacts.
3) Any special category data examples or PHI examples (to evaluate HIPAA scope).

What we will do / propose:
- I attached Redwood_DPA_template_v3.docx for your legal team to review. Our typical position: Redwood signs the DPA as Processor and we use the SCC Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) when Lyra is the Controller. If your legal team requires Redwood to be a Controller for specific features, we can map those flows and evaluate Module 1/3 mixes — Rishi (cc'd) will advise.
- We will also run the vendor questionnaire through Security for a focused SOC 2 snapshot — SOC 2 Type II report is planned to be in effect in Q3; we can share interim evidence in the short term.

Proposed next steps:
- Elena: send back the completed questionnaire by Tue Jun 22 if possible.
- Rishi / Legal: once questionnaire + DPA questions are clarified, route to procurement for DocuSign.
- Optional: 30-min follow-up with your legal team next week to walk the DPA/SCC mapping.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_template_v3.docx, Redwood_Vendor_Sec_OnePager.pdf

Thanks — I’ll coordinate timelines on our side.

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.ai
From: Elena Varga <elena@lyra.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Lyra evaluation - DPA request, SCC module guidance & questionnaire

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the succinct recap and the DPA template. A few quick answers and clarifying questions below.

1) SOC 2: we are currently in the final audit runway for SOC 2 Type II; auditors expect a final report in late Q3. For now we can provide a SOC control summary and our most recent internal security assessment (will attach).
2) HIPAA: some of our enterprise customers require HIPAA compliance. Lyra has a HIPAA-compliant offering for covered customers; we will flag the use cases that are PHI-related.
3) Controller/Processor: our legal prefers to treat Lyra as Controller for customer-provided data. We may request Redwood to accept Controller role for generated insights stored in our platform for a specific feature; I don’t have the full mapping yet.

I’ve attached the Lyra_Security_Questionnaire_2027.pdf — it’s our standard vendor questionnaire. Can you confirm which SCC module you recommend if Lyra remains Controller and Redwood remains Processor? Also:
- Can Redwood provide sample retention windows for request logs and model outputs?
- What visibility/audit logs can Lyra request for tenant-level access?

Procurement timeline: we are aligned to finish vendor diligence and legal review by July 28, so getting the DPA and SCC alignment squared away this month would be ideal.

I can set up a 30-min call next week between our GC and Rishi if that helps.

Regards,
Elena Varga
Head of Partnerships | Lyra AI
elena@lyra.ai
Attachments: Lyra_Security_Questionnaire_2027.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varga <elena@lyra.ai>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:05:30 -0700
Subject: RE: Lyra evaluation - DPA request, SCC module guidance & questionnaire

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick reply and for sending the questionnaire. I’m Rishi on Redwood Legal; looping in Laura from Security to surface any technical clarifications. A few notes from legal review perspective: 

1) DPA / SCC recommendation: Redwood’s standard position for SaaS inference is to be Processor when we receive customer data to execute inference. For that configuration, the appropriate EU SCC is the Controller-to-Processor (commonly referenced as Module 2 in the 2021 SCC modular framework). If Lyra remains Controller for the data you send into Redwood, Module 2 is the clean fit.

2) Hybrid flows: If Lyra needs Redwood to act as Controller for persistent generated artifacts (for example, summarization results stored by Redwood on your behalf), we will need to map those specific flows. In some cases a mixed-module approach is necessary — we can document a mixed controller/processor mapping and adopt the SCC modules that match each flow.

3) Needed inputs to finalize DPA: completed questionnaire (helps Security triage SAS controls), examples of any special categories / PHI, list of EU data subject regions you anticipate, and any retention limits you require.

4) Evidence & timing: SOC 2 Type II report is expected in Q3 — in the interim we can provide SOC control evidence and a short security posture memo. Laura: could you call out any high-risk control gaps we should flag to Lyra here?

Next steps proposal:
- Elena: confirm whether Lyra expects Redwood to be Processor only (preferred) or require Controller status for parts of the product, and share completed questionnaire by Tue Jun 22.
- Redwood Legal/Security: we will review questionnaire and produce a DPA redline and recommended SCC modules within 3 business days of receiving it.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call next week to go through any redlines.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_template_v3.docx (for reference).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
